p.CODKIT-DEFINITION: Codkit turns a fork upgrade into a repeatable operation, for any family of upstreams a project type describes (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-TERM`): move the upstream pin, reapply a machine-readable patch set, resolve the explicit red list, verify, and regenerate.

facts.GOAL-ANY-FORK: The same Codkit installation can operate on unrelated forks and unrelated patch sets, of one project type or of several.
facts.GOAL-VISIBLE-DELTA: Every downstream difference has an owner, reason, intervention layer, and verification evidence.
facts.GOAL-CHEAP-UPGRADE: Upgrade cost is proportional to the maintained intervention inventory, not to upstream repository history.
facts.GOAL-PORTABLE: Linux, macOS, and Windows are supported targets, and offline CI is a first-class target. A target is not accepted merely because platform-neutral code exists: native execution evidence is required.
facts.PORTABILITY-PROOF-STATUS: Linux automation proves the currently executed host. Native macOS and Windows wrapper, filesystem, Git, and regeneration runs remain open acceptance evidence until those runners execute successfully.

facts.PATCHES-ARE-TRUTH: The patch set is source of truth; the managed fork tree is reproducible working state.
facts.EDIT-IN-TREE-SAVE-TO-PATCHSET: Developers edit and test in the managed tree, then use `codkit save` to extract validated changes into the patch set.
facts.PATCH-LAST-RESORT: Codkit prefers owned modules and declarative layers; textual patches are the last intervention layer.
facts.NO-UPSTREAM-DELETION: Upstream lines are preserved; intentional changes remain attributable and reversible.
